requirement: Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` when a more precise reference is available, such as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
rationale:
**Obligations.** The subject `requirements.references.anchors.guidance` has two parts:
- Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such as one attached to the implementing or testing item.
- Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.

The first part is behavior of agents. It is not something Habeas code can check. The only testable obligation is the second: the bundled skill text must contain the direction. The cited `requirements.references.anchors` is context only and is not reassessed here.

**Test mapping.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_limit_anchors_to_files_whose_items_cannot_carry_references]` is marked `{test}` for the subject. It does the following:
- It loads the habeas skill's `references/syntax-details.md` through `skill_file`, which `include_str!`s the bundled asset.
- It extracts the `## Anchors` section with `section`, which collects the lines from that heading to the next heading of the same or a higher level.
- It uses `assert_text` to require two phrases in that section. The first is "When a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a reference". The second is "Don't anchor a file whose items can carry a reference themselves".

I searched the real asset. `assets/skills/habeas/references/syntax-details.md#section[Syntax details]/section[Anchors]` contains both phrases. It restricts anchoring to files that cannot carry a reference, such as shipped skills or copied stylesheets. It ends with "Don't anchor a file whose items can carry a reference themselves." That is the required direction in the skill's own words.

**Assertion strength.** The assertions are scoped to the Anchors section, so the text cannot pass by appearing elsewhere in the file. The test fails if either the permission condition or the prohibition is removed or reworded, and `assert_text` panics with the missing phrase. Related tests also cover how the skill text is reached. The one I read, `bundled_skills_say_when_to_read_each_reference_file`, checks the link from the habeas `SKILL.md` to `syntax-details.md`.

**Plural "skills".** The other bundled skills are `habeas-requirements`, `habeas-evidence`, `habeas-refactor` and `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`. A search of `assets/skills` for anchor guidance found nothing in them that tells agents to anchor files. `habeas-refactor` only describes rewriting anchors, and `habeas-requirements` only notes that an anchor alone supplies no implementation source. The habeas skill is the home skill for syntax, so giving the direction there satisfies the requirement. I found no scenario the test would miss.

**Gaps and acknowledgments.** I found no adequacy gap. There are no `{fixme}` acknowledgments.

text: :::{req} anchors.guidance

Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file under {cite}`requirements.references.anchors` when a more precise reference is available, such as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
For each `:test:` anchor, the harness MUST include the selected file or node's
source text in the initial model request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` and MUST record that selection
as an evidence input under {cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`,
so changing that source makes the evidence stale.
A `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT require an input selecting its source. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
